es: Reconocer cómo un titular orienta la lectura: palabras con carga emocional, verbos neutros, información destacada u omitida y tono.

teaching.en: A headline can frame a story in different ways.
teaching.es: Un titular puede dar un enfoque distinto a una misma noticia.
teaching.explanationEs: Frame: el titular orienta cómo vas a leer la noticia antes de leerla.
teaching.audioText: A headline can frame a story in different ways.

teaching.en: Words like shocking and slashed are loaded: they carry strong feelings.
teaching.es: Palabras como impactante y recortó están cargadas: llevan emociones fuertes.
teaching.explanationEs: Loaded: una palabra que añade emoción o juicio además del hecho.
segments: Words like shocking and slashed are
teaching.audioText: Words like shocking and slashed are loaded: they carry strong feelings.

teaching.en: A neutral headline says what happened without strong feelings.
teaching.es: Un titular neutral dice qué pasó sin emociones fuertes.
teaching.explanationEs: Neutral: verbos como closes o announces solo informan.
teaching.audioText: A neutral headline says what happened without strong feelings.

teaching.en: Some headlines omit the reason for the decision.
teaching.es: Algunos titulares omiten la razón de la decisión.
teaching.explanationEs: Omit: dejar fuera un dato. Lo que falta también orienta al lector.
teaching.audioText: Some headlines omit the reason for the decision.

teaching.en: The writer chose to highlight the cost, not the children.
teaching.es: El autor eligió destacar el coste, no a los niños.
teaching.explanationEs: Highlight: poner un dato en primer plano para que pese más.
teaching.audioText: The writer chose to highlight the cost, not the children.

teaching.en: The tone of the first headline is angry, and the tone of the second is calm.
teaching.es: El tono del primer titular es enfadado y el del segundo es tranquilo.
teaching.explanationEs: Tone: la actitud que transmiten las palabras elegidas.
segments: The tone of the first headline is angry,
and the tone of the second is calm.
teaching.audioText: The tone of the first headline is angry, and the tone of the second is calm.

es: Elegir el verbo de reporte (state, claim, allege, insist, admit, deny) que muestre la actitud del periodista ante lo que dice una fuente.

teaching.en: The report does not state the cause of the fire.
teaching.es: El informe no indica la causa del incendio.
teaching.explanationEs: State: declarar con formalidad, como un hecho. Es el más neutral.
teaching.audioText: The report does not state the cause of the fire.

teaching.en: Some drivers claim that the light was green.
teaching.es: Algunos conductores afirman que el semáforo estaba en verde.
teaching.explanationEs: Claim: afirma algo; el periodista se distancia un poco porque no está probado.
teaching.audioText: Some drivers claim that the light was green.

teaching.en: Police allege that the man took the bike.
teaching.es: La policía alega que el hombre se llevó la bicicleta.
teaching.explanationEs: Allege: acusa sin pruebas definitivas. Es formal y típico de la noticia judicial.
teaching.audioText: Police allege that the man took the bike.

teaching.en: Both teams insist that they played fairly.
teaching.es: Los dos equipos insisten en que jugaron limpio.
teaching.explanationEs: Insist: lo dice con firmeza, a veces repitiéndolo. Después va that.
teaching.audioText: Both teams insist that they played fairly.

teaching.en: The owner had to admit that the price was wrong.
teaching.es: El dueño tuvo que admitir que el precio era incorrecto.
teaching.explanationEs: Admit: reconoce algo negativo o incómodo para él.
teaching.audioText: The owner had to admit that the price was wrong.

teaching.en: The mayor continues to deny that the park will close.
teaching.es: El alcalde sigue negando que el parque vaya a cerrar.
teaching.explanationEs: Deny + that + oración: rechaza una acusación o un rumor.
teaching.audioText: The mayor continues to deny that the park will close.

prompt.es: ¿Qué verbo informa de forma neutral?

choices.text: alleges
insists
states

feedback.es: Un informe oficial da el dato como hecho: states. Alleges y insists añaden distancia o firmeza.

hint.es: Un informe oficial da el dato como hecho: verbo neutral.

admit

es: Comparar dos versiones de un mismo hecho y separar lo que coincide, lo que cambia en el enfoque y lo que no se puede comprobar.

teaching.en: Each outlet reports that the town market opened on Saturday.

teaching.en: This version says that two thousand people came, but the other says five thousand.
teaching.es: Esta versión dice que vinieron dos mil personas, pero la otra dice cinco mil.

teaching.en: Greedy bus company hits commuters with shocking fare rise.
teaching.es: La codiciosa empresa de autobuses golpea a los viajeros con una escandalosa subida de tarifas.
teaching.explanationEs: Titular sesgado: greedy, hits y shocking son palabras cargadas. Commuters son los viajeros habituales.
teaching.audioText: Greedy bus company hits commuters with shocking fare rise.

teaching.en: The bus company announces a fare rise of ten per cent.
teaching.es: La empresa de autobuses anuncia una subida de tarifas del diez por ciento.

prompt.es: Escribe la noticia neutral: titular, cifras y dos fuentes atribuidas.

answer.text: City council raises parking fee to two dollars an hour. From the first of March, the fee will rise from one dollar to two dollars an hour. A council spokesperson says that maintenance costs have risen. According to a residents' association, the new fee is too high for small shops. The association also says that some customers may stop coming. The council and the association give different reasons, and the effect on shop sales has not been confirmed.
accepted: City council raises parking fee to two dollars an hour. From the first of March, the fee will rise from one dollar to two dollars an hour. A council spokesperson says that maintenance costs have risen. According to a residents' association, the new fee is too high for small shops. es: Examinar una publicación viral, contrastarla con dos fuentes y explicar a un amigo qué es fiable y qué no, con certeza graduada.

teaching.en: This viral post says that all schools will close for two weeks.
teaching.es: Esta publicación viral dice que todos los colegios cerrarán dos semanas.
teaching.explanationEs: Viral: se comparte muy deprisa. Que sea viral no la hace cierta.

schools will close for two weeks.

teaching.en: The post has no source, and it tells you to share it quickly.
teaching.es: La publicación no tiene fuente y te dice que la compartas rápido.
teaching.explanationEs: Señales de sesgo: ninguna fuente y presión para compartir (share now).
segments: The post has no source, and it
tells you to share it quickly.

teaching.en: A reliable source, like the school office, can verify the news.

teaching.explanationEs: Reliable: se puede confiar en ella. Verify: comprobar si algo es cierto.

teaching.en: The local radio says that only one school will close, so the post is probably a rumour.
teaching.es: La radio local dice que solo un colegio cerrará, así que la publicación probablemente es un rumor.
teaching.explanationEs: Rumour: noticia sin confirmar que circula entre la gente. Se contrasta con otra fuente.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la mejor respuesta para explicar la conclusión a un amigo?

choices.text: I checked two sources, and the post is 100 per cent false, no doubt.
I checked nothing, but everybody shares it, so it is true.
I checked two sources, and they disagree with the post, so it may well be a rumour.

feedback.es: La respuesta que cita dos fuentes contrastadas y gradúa la certeza (may well) es la adecuada. Afirmar 100 % de certeza exagera, y no comprobar nada y fiarse de que todos la comparten no prueba nada.

prompt.es: Explica a un amigo si fiarse de la publicación: sesgo, dos fuentes y conclusión graduada.

answer.text: Hi Sam, I do not think that post is reliable. First, it uses urgent words like URGENT and SHARE NOW, and it does not give a source. Second, I checked two sources. The shop website says that it is not giving away free bikes. The local radio says that there is only a ten per cent offer for students. Given that both sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real. It may well be a rumour, so please do not share it until we can verify it.
accepted: Hi Sam, I do not think that post is reliable. First, it uses urgent words like URGENT and SHARE NOW, and it does not give a source. Second, I checked two sources. The shop website says that it is not giving away free bikes. The local radio says that there is only a ten per cent offer for students. Given that both sources disagree with the post, it is unlikely that the offer is real. It may well be a rumour, so please do not share it until we can verify it.

Sam, I would not trust that post. It has no source, and words like URGENT and SHARE NOW try to make you act quickly. I checked the shop website, and it says that there is no offer of free bikes. The local radio only mentions a ten per cent offer for students. Because two reliable sources disagree with the post, it is probably a rumour. I cannot be completely sure, but I suggest that we wait and verify it before we share it.

feedback.es: La explicación a un amigo nombra señales de sesgo, contrasta dos fuentes y concluye con certeza graduada.
